answer: One concrete mechanism: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because marble only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, river is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any lantern approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
